title: Linking a Customized Employment Intervention to Life Satisfaction of Individuals with Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities: The Mediating Role of Integrated Employment
abstract: This study examined the effect of a Customized Employment (CE) intervention on the life satisfaction of individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) through the mediation of integrated employment (number of jobs in the past 12 months). A randomized controlled trial was conducted in Spain with unemployed individuals with IDD who were randomly assigned to control (N = 202) or experimental (N = 232) groups. The CE intervention took place from September 2022 to July 2023. Life satisfaction and employment were measured at baseline (September–October 2022), mid-intervention, and follow-up (December 2023–January 2024). Results confirmed the mediation process: individuals in the experimental group secured more jobs than controls, and this integrated employment was in turn associated with higher life satisfaction. These findings elucidate the mechanism through which CE exerts its effects, specifically by improving integrated employment, which in turn enhances life satisfaction.
